grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('chakapwanyika')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'chakapwanyika' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('ruvara')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'ruvara'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Counting & Numbers in Shona ('imwe')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, number words like 'imwe' always come AFTER the noun they count, and their starting prefix matches the noun's group! The basic number stems are: '-mwe' (1), '-viri' (2), '-tatu' (3), '-na' (4), and '-shanu' (5). For example, when counting people ('vanhu'), you use 'va-': 'munhu mumwe' (1 person), 'vanhu vaviri' (2 people), 'varume vana' (4 men). When counting 'ma-' plurals like 'maminitsi' (minutes) or 'mavara' (colours), you use 'ma-': 'madhongi maviri' (2 donkeys), 'mavara matatu' (3 colours), 'maminitsi mashanu' (5 minutes).
grammar_notes.rule: Noun + Number Stem (-mwe = 1, -viri = 2, -tatu = 3, -na = 4, -shanu = 5) -> vanhu vaviri (2 people), maminitsi mashanu (5 minutes)

cultural_notes.title: Shona Cultural & Everyday Context (Lesson 1)
cultural_notes.content: This expression ('Chidziro chakapwanyika pane imwe nzvimbo.Mukati mechidziro mune miti yakawanda ine ruvara rwegirini poita muti umwe chete wemujakaranda wakatumbuka maruva ane ruvara rwepeporo.Kunze kwechidziro kune huswa hwakaoma.' — "Thing dziro chakapwanyika on / at ne imwe nzvimbo.mukati mechidziro in / singular ne trees it (past) wanda ine colour rwegirini poita tree umwe chete wemujakaranda you/he (past) tumbuka.") reflects how Shona speakers connect daily family life, work, and community relationships across urban towns and rural homesteads ('kumusha') in Zimbabwe.

active_exercises.prompt: If a farmer says 'Gore rino takawana goho guru pamunda pedu', what happened?
options: They are waiting for the rain to start next month
The river flooded and washed away the bridge
A strong wind blew from the east all afternoon
They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.correct_answer: They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.explanation: 'Takawana' = 'we obtained/got', 'goho guru' = 'a big harvest', 'pamunda pedu' = 'from our field'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta uye mvura ichanaya manheru.'
options: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
The river is full of water after yesterday's heavy rain.
Tall green trees grow along the sides of the mountain.
The dog barked outside when it saw the visitors.
active_exercises.correct_answer: The wind is blowing and it will rain in the evening.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mhepo iri kuvhuvhuta' = 'The wind is blowing', 'uye' = 'and', 'mvura ichanaya manheru' = 'it will rain in the evening'.

active_exercises.prompt: What is the difference between 'mumba' and 'panze'?
options: 'mumba' means at school, while 'panze' means at work
'mumba' means inside the house, while 'panze' means outside
'mumba' means on the roof, while 'panze' means in the kitchen
'mumba' means rural village, while 'panze' means city centre
active_exercises.correct_answer: 'mumba' means inside the house, while 'panze' means outside
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' denotes 'inside' ('mumba' = inside the house), whereas 'panze' means 'outside in the yard'.
